summary: Tested the email rate-limit (429) retry fix. Unit tests with mocked httpx: 9/9 passed. A 429 followed by 200 succeeds with a 2s backoff. Backoff runs 2,4,8s, uses Retry-After when given and caps it at 15s. Four 429s in a row give 503 with the Swedish rate-limit message. 422, 500 and 402 insufficient_credits are not retried. send_order_reply shows the 503 text and the generic message for other errors. Integration: 4/4 passed with 2 real emails to delivered@resend.dev (both 202). The email-link POST /api/order-reply/{token} returned the 'Svar skickat' page and set order B10031 to confirmed. The admin reply POST /api/admin/orders/{id}/reply returned 200 with no confirm_token or _id. Frontend (375x667): Alla ordrar -> B10031 -> reply sheet. A mocked 400 rate-limit response shows the new clear message in reply-error. One real send returned 200, closed the sheet, showed the toast and set status to BEKRÄFTAD. 3 real emails in total, all to delivered@resend.dev. No new order was placed, so no email went to prii_de@hotmail.com, and order_email was left unchanged. No deprecated Expo packages found.

minor.issue: It retries on every HTTP 429, whatever the error code. If the provider ever sends daily_limit_reached or another non-burst code as 429, the request waits about 14s for nothing before returning the 503 'E-post är tillfälligt otillgänglig'. Suggestion: retry only when the body code is 'rate_limited'.

Pre-existing behaviour: if the order email is still rate-limited after retries, the order is saved with email_status=failed. There is no admin or background way to resend the order email to the recipient.

action_items: Optional: in emailer.send_email, retry only when the 429 body code == 'rate_limited'
Optional: add a way to resend the order email for orders with email_status=failed
critical_code_review_comments: Retry/backoff logic is correct: attempt 0..3, then raise_for_status on the final response -> HTTPStatusError -> 503 with the rate-limit message. Worst-case added latency is about 14s plus 4 HTTP calls, which is fine within the ingress timeout.
send_order_reply passes every 503 detail through (rate limit and 'tillfälligt otillgänglig') and maps other errors to the generic text. The HTML reply form escapes the error message.
seed_data_creation: No new orders. The existing order B10031 (id bc22a5ef-b42a-4ec7-9a89-31924b742504, delivered@resend.dev) now has 3 TEST_ replies and status confirmed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The unit test mocks httpx.AsyncClient.post and asyncio.sleep, so it sends no real emails. The integration test sends 2 real emails to delivered@resend.dev via order B10031 (MAX_REPLIES=10, now 3 used). Set env ITER7_ORDER_ID to use another order. Avoid bursts of real emails. In Playwright, wait about 1.5s after the reply sheet opens (slide animation) before clicking reply-send-button.
